To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CDKs phosphorylate Smad3, thereby inhibiting its transcriptional activity, which in turn leads to the inactivation of the Smad3 antiproliferation pathway.

the CDK4 and cyclin D1 are required for the growth of human cancers and that CDK4 phosphorylation of the Rb family and Smad3 inhibitory proteins is a mechanism by which CDK4 and other CDKs contribute to the malignant growth of human cancers.
CDK phosphorylation inactivates Smad3 and Rb and that CDK phosphorylates Rb in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how CDKs regulate the activity of Rb and Smad proteins.
the role of the CDK-Rb family of proteins in regulating the cell cycle.
the molecular mechanism by which CDKs regulate the activity of Rb and Smad family members and the biological consequences of CDK phosphorylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Smad3 and Rb family members are the major CDK targets and that the CDK phosphorylation inhibits the antiproliferation function of Smad and Rb proteins in cancer.
CDKs are not only important in cell cycle regulation, but also play a critical role in cell growth and differentiation.
CDK4/CDK6 phosphorylate Rb family members, thereby inhibiting their tumor suppressive functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDKs phosphorylate Rb, p107 and Smad3, all of which are tumor suppressors, and thereby contribute to tumor development and/or progression.
CDKs are important for cell cycle progression and also for the control of cell proliferation by the TGF- β pathway.

the Rb family of pocket proteins are not only substrates of CDk4, but Smad3 is also a substrate of CDK4 and 2 and that the phosphorylation of Smads by these CDKs may provide a mechanism for the inhibition of Smad function during early stages of tumourigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CDK4/6 can phosphorylate and inactivate Smad proteins and this may contribute to tumorgenesis.
CDK phosphorylation may be an important mechanism by which the Rb and Smad pathways are linked and that the Rb and TGF-β pathways may have overlapping roles in tumor suppression.
CDK4 and 2 phosphorylate Smad3 and inhibit its antiproliferation function.
